To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Grid tools developed by CMS and by LCG can be used to support CMS distributed data analysis and that the CMS analysis system can be used to run CMS distributed analysis.
the CMS analysis system is based on the use of Grid tools, and that CMS will use both LCG-2 and ARDA tools to achieve the goals.

the CMS distributed analysis system will be based on the LCG-1 release and that it is possible to develop a system to access the CMS distributed analysis farm with a user-friendly interface, based on the LFC, the LCG-Bookkeeping and the ARDA project.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the Grid tools to support the CMS distributed analysis, with a particular emphasis on the user interface.
the use of Grid tools to access data and resources in order to perform distributed data analysis.

the following issues: - How to provide a transparent access to data and computing resources, hiding the complexity of the Grid tools and providing a user-friendly environment to the physicists; - How to provide the possibility of running the analysis on a local machine, on a local farm or on a remote farm, depending on the user needs and the availability of resources; - How to manage the large number of jobs that will be running on the Grid, and how to provide a mechanism to monitor the status of the jobs
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CMS analysis system is a working system that can be used for the analysis of CMS data and that is being improved and developed further to be ready for the start of data taking in 2007.
CMS is making good progress in the development of its analysis system and in particular in the integration of the Grid tools in its software framework.
the CMS distributed analysis system is working and that the analysis system has been used by the CMS collaboration to perform physics analyses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CMS distributed analysis system is now operational and is being intensively used by CMS physicists.
the CMS analysis system is now able to access the data from the LHC computing centres, to submit the jobs to the LHC Computing Grid and to monitor the progress of the job submission and execution.
CMS is now able to submit and monitor large scale jobs using Grid tools, and is working on the development of the user interfaces and the integration with the CMS software framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to use Grid tools to perform distributed data analysis, even if the data size is of the order of 200 TB.
the Grid tools are mature enough to allow the development of a distributed analysis system for the CMS experiment.
the CMS experiment will have a Grid-based analysis system in place by the end of 2006, and will use it in the first phase of data taking.
